name: VICI Properties Inc
reason: Durable triple-net gaming leases but consensus FFO growth of 5.9%/7.7%/3.1% and LTG ~2% give no route to 7%+ per-share growth, with net debt/EBITDA 4.7x and heavy Caesars/MGM tenant concentration.

name: Merchants Bancorp
reason: Spread- and credit-driven multifamily/warehouse lender whose EPS fell 40% in 2025 to 0.6x its 2024 peak, signalling credit-cycle exposure rather than a low-cost-deposit franchise.

name: Core Natural Resources, Inc.
reason: Coal producer with earnings set by met/thermal coal prices (EPS swung from 19.79 in 2023 to -2.98 in 2025) and long-run secular decline in thermal demand.

name: Newmark Group, Inc.
reason: Commercial real estate brokerage/capital-markets business tied to transaction cycles, with 4.2x net debt/EBITDA, shares up 5.1%/yr and an adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap of ~181%.

name: ZoomInfo Technologies Inc
reason: B2B contact-data platform facing credible AI disintermediation, with consensus EPS growth of only 3%/0.5%/4%, a ~422% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and 3.9x net debt/EBITDA.

name: Everforth, Inc.
reason: IT staffing/consulting (ex-ASGN) with EPS down to 0.69x its 2022 peak, EBIT margin in the 9th percentile of its history, acquisitive growth (acq/FCF 0.76) and exposure to AI-driven pressure on billable IT work.

name: Victory Capital Holdings, Inc.
reason: Acquisition-built active asset manager (acq/FCF 0.67) whose fees track markets, with secular outflows from active funds and EBIT margin at the 90th percentile of its history.

name: Equitable Holdings, Inc.
reason: Life/annuity insurer with opaque legacy variable-annuity guarantees, negative 10y average ROE (-2.3%) and earnings sensitive to rates and equity markets, so 5-10 year earnings cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc.
reason: Asset-light economy-hotel franchisor, but EPS is at its 10y high with EBIT margin at the 91st percentile and net debt/EBITDA at 4.3x, too much leverage for a travel-cyclical business.

name: Coastal Financial Corporation
reason: Banking-as-a-service growth (EPS CAGR 19.6% over 5y) depends on fintech partners and regulatory tolerance, and consensus sees FY1 EPS -60%, so the earnings path is not forecastable.

name: Arlo Technologies, Inc.
reason: Consumer camera hardware moving to subscriptions with only 3 profitable years, a 10y average EBIT margin of -11.5% and a ~417% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap, so there is no record to forecast from.

name: Garrett Motion Inc
reason: Turbocharger maker facing structural decline as vehicles electrify, with EPS at 0.43x its 10y peak, shares up 10.6%/yr since emerging from bankruptcy, and auto-cycle exposure.

name: Diversified Energy Company
reason: Appalachian gas producer with commodity-driven earnings (EPS ranged from -14.37 to 8.40) that grew through acquisitions (acq/FCF 3.6x, shares +43%/yr) and carries 4.3x net debt/EBITDA.

name: Resideo Technologies, Inc.
reason: Spin-off with a 10y average ROIC of 1.8%, 3.2x net debt/EBITDA and an ongoing ADI distribution separation, so the business that remains cannot yet be forecast.

name: Aveanna Healthcare Holdings Inc
reason: Home-care provider dependent on Medicaid reimbursement, with EPS first positive only in 2025, growth from acquisitions (acq/FCF 7.4x) and 4.5x net debt/EBITDA.

name: Worthington Steel, Inc.
reason: Steel processor whose earnings follow steel prices and auto volumes, with EPS collapsing 92% in FY2025 to 0.05x its peak and thin 3.8% EBIT margins.

name: Ardent Health, Inc.
reason: Acute-care hospital operator exposed to government reimbursement and payer-mix risk, with a 5.1% EBIT margin, acquisition-led growth (acq/FCF 5.9x) and a 10y average ROIC of -0.3%.

name: Levi Strauss & Co.
reason: Iconic brand but revenue CAGR is only 3.4% over 10y and EBIT margin sits at the 91st percentile of its history, a good but not special apparel business with fashion and tariff risk.

name: Fox Corporation
reason: Strong balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 0.9x) and buybacks, but cash flows rest on linear-TV affiliate fees that cord-cutting erodes and on rising sports-rights costs, so 10-year earnings are hard to underwrite.

name: Driven Brands Holdings, Inc.
reason: PE-sponsored auto-services roll-up with net debt/EBITDA of 7.1x, a 10y average ROIC of -2.1% and a ~645% adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap.
